To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found no evidence for association between the tested SNPs in 5′flanking regions of ADIPOQ, LEP and RETN genes and obesity in a cohort of 243 Polish obese children and adolescent.
polymorphisms in 13 SNPs and 1 InDels in the 5′- flanking regions of ADIPOQ, LEP, and RETN genes are not associated with childhood and adolescent obesity in the Polish population.
we found no consistent evidence of association between obesity and SNPs demonstrating MAF above 0.20 (ADIPOQ, LEP and RETN genes).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for genetic markers associated with obesity and its complications in children and adolescents.
the search for genetic polymorphisms that are related to the development of obesity and its comorbidities in children and adolescents.
the role of polymorphisms in the genes encoding adipokines in childhood obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polymorphisms in 3′-UTR, intronic regions and 5′-UTR of the ADIPOQ gene are not associated with BMI and obesity in Polish population of children and adolescents.
the polymorphism in the 5′- flanking region of ADIPOQ, LEP and RETN are not associated with childhood obesity in the Polish population, however, further studies are necessary to clarify this issue.
the polymorphisms of ADIPOQ, LEP and RETN 5′-regulatory regions are not associated with childhood and adolescent obesity in Polish population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tested polymorphisms do not contribute to the obesity in Polish population and thus are not useful for genetic diagnosis of obesity.
the tested polymorphisms in ADIPOQ, LEP, and RETN are not associated with childhood and adolescence obesity and do not influence BMI in obese patients.
the 5′-UTR regions of the genes encoding adiponects, leptins, and resistins are not associated with the risk of obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5′-regions of the ADIPOQ, LEP and RETN genes in the Polish population have not undergone strong positive selection and are not associated with BMI and RBMI in obese children and adolescents.
the 5′-region of the ADIPOQ gene, which is the most promising region for the identification of obesity-associated polymorphisms, is not associated with childhood obesity in the Polish population.
the search for genetic factors predisposing to childhood and adolescent obesity should continue.
